subject: biology
name: Biology

pillars.name: Concepts
pillars.scope: The student holds a wrong idea about living things: evolution, genetics, cells, energy and matter in systems.

pillars.name: Strategy & Setup
pillars.scope: The ideas are sound, but the reasoning is set up wrongly: the wrong inheritance pattern, cross, process or experimental design, or a conclusion the data can't support.

pillars.name: Procedure
pillars.scope: The plan is right, but carrying out a method goes wrong (Punnett squares, probability rules, transcription and translation, magnification, data processing, keys).

pillars.name: Calculation & Recall
pillars.scope: Reasoning is sound; a term, structure label, sequence, fact, number, unit or rounding slips. In biology most FAC errors are recall, not arithmetic.

pillars.name: Communication
pillars.scope: The biology may be right, but the answer is not what was asked, uses loose or wrong notation, or is not explained.

pillars.name: Test Habits
pillars.scope: How the student handles the test: blanks, traps, giving up, not checking, not using provided tables.

decision_order: Is the student's idea of the biology wrong (CON)?
Is the idea right but the pattern, cross, process, design or conclusion set up wrongly (STR)?
Is the set-up right but a step of the method done wrongly (PRC)?
Is it a slip in a term, label, sequence, fact, number or unit (FAC)?
Is the biology right but the answer not what was asked, in wrong notation, or unexplained (COM)?
Or is it how the test was handled (TST)?

codes.name: Need Drives Evolution
codes.plain_name: Thinks living things change because they need to
codes.student_help: Variation exists first; the environment then selects which variants survive and reproduce.
codes.description: Explains evolution as organisms changing because they need or want to (teleology), rather than selection acting on existing variation.
codes.example: 'Giraffes grew long necks because they needed to reach high leaves.'

tell_apart.how: If the student says traits gained during life are passed on, use CON_ACQUIRED_TRAITS.
If the student understands selection but writes 'adapted to' loosely, use COM_IMPRECISE_TERMS.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: variation-then-selection simulation (bead or beak lab).

codes.name: Acquired Traits Inherited
codes.plain_name: Thinks traits gained during life are inherited
codes.student_help: Only changes in the DNA of sex cells can be passed to offspring.
codes.description: Believes characteristics gained during an organism's life (muscles, scars, learned behaviour) are passed to offspring, or that individuals evolve.
codes.example: 'A bodybuilder's children will be born more muscular.'

tell_apart.how: If the explanation rests on need or purpose, use CON_NEED_DRIVES_EVOLUTION.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: germline vs body cell diagram.

codes.name: Gene, Allele, Chromosome Scale
codes.plain_name: Mixed up genes, alleles and chromosomes
codes.student_help: DNA makes up chromosomes; a gene is a section of a chromosome; alleles are versions of a gene.
codes.description: Confuses DNA, gene, allele and chromosome, or the sizes they come in (a gene contains chromosomes; alleles are different genes).
codes.example: 'Each allele contains many chromosomes.'

tell_apart.how: If the student knows the relationships and only swaps two words, use FAC_TERM_RECALL.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: nested zoom diagram from cell to base pair.

codes.name: Dominant Means Common
codes.plain_name: Thinks dominant means common or stronger
codes.student_help: Dominant only means the allele shows when one copy is present; it says nothing about how common or how good it is.
codes.description: Believes dominant alleles are more frequent in the population, better for the organism, or will spread over time.
codes.example: 'Polydactyly is dominant, so most people have six fingers.'

tell_apart.how: If the student misidentifies which pattern applies to a cross, use STR_INHERITANCE_PATTERN.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: allele frequency counter-examples.

codes.name: Plant Respiration and Mass
codes.plain_name: Mixed up photosynthesis and respiration in plants
codes.student_help: Plants carry out cellular respiration all the time; most of their mass comes from CO₂ in the air.
codes.description: Believes plants photosynthesise instead of respiring, respire only at night, or get most of their mass from soil or water.
codes.example: 'Plants don't need cellular respiration because they make their own food.'

tell_apart.how: If the error is about energy or matter moving through an ecosystem, use CON_ENERGY_MATTER_CYCLING.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: van Helmont willow-tree analysis.

codes.name: Energy and Matter Cycling
codes.plain_name: Mixed up how energy and matter move
codes.student_help: Matter cycles through ecosystems; energy flows through once and leaves as heat.
codes.description: Believes energy is recycled in ecosystems, that matter is turned into energy, or that decomposers 'make energy'.
codes.example: 'Decomposers return energy to the soil so plants can use it again.'

tell_apart.how: If the error is specifically about plant respiration or where plant mass comes from, use CON_PLANT_MATTER_ENERGY.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: two-colour diagram (matter loops, energy arrows exit).

codes.name: Diffusion and Osmosis Direction
codes.plain_name: Got the direction of diffusion or osmosis wrong
codes.student_help: Particles spread from high to low concentration; in osmosis water moves toward the side with more solute.
codes.description: Predicts movement against the concentration gradient, thinks water moves toward lower solute concentration, or describes particles as 'wanting' to move.
codes.example: 'In salt water the cell gains water because salt pulls water out of the beaker.'

tell_apart.how: If the idea is right but a step in the comparison is skipped, use PRC_STEP_OMITTED.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: concentration-gradient sketch with arrows.

codes.name: Enzyme Function
codes.student_help: Enzymes have an optimum; past it, their shape changes (denatures) and activity drops; they are not alive.
codes.description: Believes enzymes are alive and are 'killed', that more heat always means faster enzyme activity, or that enzymes are used up in reactions.
codes.example: 'At 80 °C the enzyme works fastest because heat always speeds up reactions.'

tell_apart.how: If the idea is right but the rate is read from the graph wrongly, use PRC_DATA_PROCESSING.

codes.remediation: Tier 1: lock-and-key model with a melted key.

codes.name: Wrong Inheritance Pattern
codes.student_help: Check the clues: is it sex-linked, codominant, incomplete, or simple dominant?
codes.description: Treats a trait with the wrong pattern: sex-linked as autosomal, codominance as incomplete dominance, multiple alleles as two alleles.
codes.example: Colour-blindness cross done with autosomal alleles Bb × bb.

tell_apart.how: If the pattern is right but the parent genotypes are wrong, use STR_CROSS_SETUP.
If the student misunderstands what dominance means, use CON_DOMINANT_MEANS_COMMON.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: pattern clue checklist.

codes.name: Cross Set Up Wrongly
codes.plain_name: Started the cross with the wrong parents
codes.student_help: Turn each word description into a genotype before you draw the square.
codes.description: Uses the right pattern but the wrong parent genotypes or gametes from the description (heterozygous written as homozygous, a carrier not shown).
codes.example: 'A heterozygous tall plant crossed with a short plant' set up as TT × tt.

tell_apart.how: If the pattern is wrong, use STR_INHERITANCE_PATTERN.
If the parents are right and the square is filled wrongly, use PRC_PUNNETT_SQUARE.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: description-to-genotype table.

codes.name: Wrong Process Identified
codes.student_help: Ask what the result needs to be (identical cells? gametes? protein?) and choose the process that makes it.
codes.description: Applies the wrong process to the situation: mitosis for gamete formation, transcription where translation is meant, respiration for photosynthesis, active transport for diffusion.
codes.example: 'Sperm cells are made by mitosis, so they have 46 chromosomes.'

tell_apart.how: If the student describes the right process but uses the wrong name for it, use FAC_TERM_RECALL.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: process comparison table.

codes.name: Pedigree Reasoning Error
codes.plain_name: Drew the wrong conclusion from the pedigree
codes.student_help: Look for two unaffected parents with an affected child (recessive) or a pattern only in males (X-linked).
codes.description: Draws the inheritance pattern from a pedigree without the key test (unaffected parents with an affected child, male-only patterns, father-to-son passing).
codes.example: Calls a trait dominant because it appears in every generation, though two unaffected parents have an affected child.

tell_apart.how: STR_INHERITANCE_PATTERN is for using the wrong pattern in a cross; this code is for misreading a pedigree to find it.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: pedigree decision steps.

codes.name: Correlation as Cause
codes.plain_name: Said one thing causes another from a pattern alone
codes.student_help: A pattern shows a link; cause needs a controlled experiment or a mechanism.
codes.description: Concludes cause from a correlation, generalises beyond the sample, or ignores a likely third factor.
codes.example: 'Cities with more hospitals have more deaths, so hospitals cause deaths.'

tell_apart.how: COM_OBSERVATION_VS_INFERENCE is about where statements go in a report; this code is about the logic of the conclusion.
If the flaw is in how the experiment was planned, use STR_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: 'what else could explain this?' prompt.

codes.name: Ignored Condition
codes.student_help: A condition the question gave was not used, like 'x is positive' or a point on the line.
codes.description: Leaves a stated condition or given piece of information out of the model, so the answer does not meet it.
codes.example: Question says the mother is a carrier; student uses XᴴXᴴ.

tell_apart.how: If the condition was read wrongly rather than left out, use TST_MISREAD_GIVEN.
If the condition is used but turned into the wrong genotype, use STR_CROSS_SETUP.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: condition checklist.

codes.name: No Viable Plan
codes.student_help: The first move here could not lead to the answer. Plan the method before writing.
codes.description: Starts with a move that cannot reach the answer, or moves symbols around with no method.
codes.example: Asked for the probability of a child with both traits, draws three unrelated Punnett squares with no plan to combine them.

tell_apart.how: If there is only an answer with no work, use TST_UNWORKED_GUESS; this code needs visible work that wanders.

codes.remediation: Plan-first prompt: name the target, the known quantities and the bridge between them before calculating.

codes.name: Experimental Design Flaw
codes.student_help: Change one thing, measure one thing, and keep everything else the same.
codes.description: Gets the independent, dependent or controlled variables wrong, leaves out a control or repeats, or designs a test that cannot answer the question.
codes.example: Tests a fertiliser on one plant in sunlight and a control plant in shade.

tell_apart.how: This code is about how the experiment is set up; COM_OBSERVATION_VS_INFERENCE is about how the results are reported.
STR_NO_VIABLE_PLAN is for calculation problems; use this code for planning an investigation.

codes.remediation: Fair-test frame: I will change ___, measure ___, and keep ___ the same; repeat ___ times.

codes.name: Step Omission
codes.student_help: A needed step in the method was skipped.
codes.description: Skips a required step of the procedure, so the result does not follow.
codes.example: Calculates actual cell size without first finding the field of view at the higher magnification.

tell_apart.how: Here a middle step is missing and the answer is wrong; in PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION the work is right but stops before the end.
If the plan itself is missing, use STR_NO_VIABLE_PLAN; here the plan is right and one step drops out.

codes.remediation: Faded worked example: complete the one missing step in an otherwise finished solution.

codes.name: Punnett Square Error
codes.plain_name: Filled in the Punnett square wrongly
codes.student_help: Split each parent into gametes along the edges, then combine one from each side in every box.
codes.description: Splits gametes wrongly (Tt into TT), combines boxes wrongly, or counts the ratio wrongly from a correct square.
codes.example: For a dihybrid cross, lists gametes TtRr instead of TR, Tr, tR, tr.

tell_apart.how: If the parents are wrong before the square, use STR_CROSS_SETUP.
If the square is right but probabilities are combined wrongly afterwards, use PRC_PROBABILITY_RULES.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: gamete-first worked example.

codes.name: Probability Rules Misapplied
codes.student_help: Use 'and' → multiply; 'or' → add, for separate events.
codes.description: Adds probabilities that should be multiplied (independent events) or multiplies ones that should be added; treats each child as affecting the next.
codes.example: Chance of two affected children = ¼ + ¼ = ½.

tell_apart.how: If the error is inside the Punnett square, use PRC_PUNNETT_SQUARE.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: and/or rule card.

codes.name: Transcription / Translation Error
codes.plain_name: Made a mistake copying DNA to RNA or protein
codes.student_help: RNA uses U instead of T; read codons in threes from the start codon using the mRNA, not the DNA.
codes.description: Pairs bases wrongly, keeps T in mRNA, reads codons from the DNA or the wrong strand, or shifts the reading frame.
codes.example: Transcribes DNA TAC GGA as mRNA ATG CCT.

tell_apart.how: If the student does the wrong process altogether, use STR_WRONG_PROCESS.
If one base is miscopied between lines, use FAC_COPY_ERROR.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: base-pairing template with a codon ruler.

codes.name: Magnification Calculation Error
codes.plain_name: Worked out the magnification or size wrongly
codes.student_help: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective; at higher power the field of view shrinks by the same factor.
codes.description: Multiplies where it should divide, adds eyepiece and objective, or scales the field of view the wrong way.
codes.example: Field of view 4 mm at 40×: says it is 16 mm at 400×.

tell_apart.how: If the method is right and mm to µm goes wrong, use FAC_UNIT_CONVERSION.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: magnification ratio table.

codes.name: Data Processing Error
codes.plain_name: Processed or graphed the data wrongly
codes.student_help: Choose the graph type for the data, use an even scale, and take rates from the slope.
codes.description: Processes data wrongly: wrong graph type, uneven scale, rate taken from a single point, averages that include an outlier without comment.
codes.example: Plots enzyme rate against temperature as a bar graph with uneven gaps on the x-axis.

tell_apart.how: If the graph is right but missing title or axis labels, use COM_MISSING_LABELS.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: data-handling checklist.

codes.name: Classification Key Error
codes.plain_name: Used the key or classification order wrongly
codes.student_help: Follow the key one choice at a time; the order is domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.
codes.description: Skips couplets in a dichotomous key, writes a key with overlapping choices, or orders taxonomic ranks wrongly; formats binomial names wrongly.
codes.example: Writes the scientific name as 'Homo Sapiens'.

tell_apart.how: If only the order of ranks is misremembered, use FAC_SEQUENCE_RECALL.

codes.remediation: Tier 2: key-walk practice with a real specimen set.

codes.name: Stopped Before the End
codes.student_help: Read the question again when you think you are done: is your last line the thing it asked for?
codes.description: Correct work that stops before the requested quantity or form is reached.
codes.example: Asked for the phenotype ratio, gives the genotype ratio from the square and stops.

tell_apart.how: If the student aimed at a different target from the start, use COM_ANSWERED_DIFFERENT_QUESTION; here they were heading to the right target and stopped.
If an intermediate value is boxed as if it were final, use TST_DISTRACTOR_TRAP; if the work simply ends, use this code.

codes.remediation: Completion checklist: target quantity, unit, form asked for.

codes.name: Arithmetic Slip
codes.student_help: The steps make sense, with a small calculation slip in the numbers.
codes.description: An isolated arithmetic error with a sound method.
codes.example: Calculates 400 ÷ 40 as 100.

tell_apart.how: If the magnification method is wrong (multiplying where it should divide), use PRC_MAGNIFICATION; this code is for a slip in the numbers.

codes.remediation: Five-item rapid micro-drill on the same operation.

codes.name: Copy Error
codes.student_help: A number or sign changed when copying from one line to the next.
codes.description: Miscopies a digit, sign or term from one of the student's own lines to the next.
codes.example: Copies the mRNA AUG CCA as AUG CAC on the next line.

tell_apart.how: If the value was read wrongly from the question itself, use TST_MISREAD_GIVEN; this code is for copying between the student's own lines.
If a value was calculated wrongly rather than copied, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Line-to-line check habit.

codes.name: Unit Conversion
codes.student_help: A unit conversion was off, like centimetres to metres.
codes.description: Converts units wrongly or mixes units in one calculation.
codes.example: Converts 0.4 mm to 40 µm.

tell_apart.how: Here the number is wrong because of a conversion; in COM_MISSING_UNITS the number is right but the unit is not written.
If the conversion factor is right and the multiplication goes wrong, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Dimensional conversion bridge: write the factor as a fraction that cancels the old unit.

codes.name: Rounding / Precision
codes.student_help: A number was rounded too early or to the wrong decimal place.
codes.description: Rounds too early, or breaks the precision the question asks for.
codes.example: Reports mean heart rate as 72.3333 bpm.

tell_apart.how: If the digits themselves are wrong, not just how many are kept, use FAC_ARITHMETIC_SLIP.

codes.remediation: Precision rules card: count significant figures in the givens, keep guard digits, round once.

codes.name: Term Recall Slip
codes.student_help: Check terms that sound alike (mitosis/meiosis, ileum/ilium, xylem/phloem).
codes.description: Knows the idea but uses the wrong technical word for it, often a similar-sounding term.
codes.example: 'Water travels up the stem in the phloem.'

tell_apart.how: If the swap shows a wrong idea of how the terms relate, use the concept code.
If the student uses an everyday word instead of a technical one, use COM_IMPRECISE_TERMS.

codes.remediation: Tier 3: paired-term flash cards.

codes.name: Structure Label Slip
codes.student_help: Check each label line ends exactly on the part it names.
codes.description: Labels a part of a diagram (cell, organ, heart, flower) with the wrong name, or points the line at the wrong part.
codes.example: Labels the left ventricle as the right ventricle on a heart diagram.

tell_apart.how: If labels are missing rather than wrong, use COM_MISSING_LABELS.

codes.remediation: Tier 3: blank-diagram labelling drill.

codes.name: Sequence Recall Slip
codes.plain_name: Put the stages in the wrong order
codes.student_help: Use a memory aid (PMAT; right atrium → right ventricle → lungs) and check each step.
codes.description: Gets the order of stages or a pathway wrong (phases of mitosis, blood flow, digestion, Krebs before glycolysis).
codes.example: Lists the mitosis phases as prophase, anaphase, metaphase, telophase.

tell_apart.how: If the wrong process is used entirely, use STR_WRONG_PROCESS.

codes.remediation: Tier 3: sequencing cards.

codes.name: Fact Recall Slip
codes.student_help: Check this fact in your notes; it is one to memorise.
codes.description: Misremembers a specific fact: which acids are strong, valence electrons for a group, a solubility rule, a functional group name.
codes.example: 'Human gametes have 46 chromosomes.'

tell_apart.how: If the wrong number comes from picking the wrong process (mitosis for gametes), use STR_WRONG_PROCESS.

codes.remediation: Tier 3: spaced-recall quiz on the fact list.

codes.name: Answered a Different Question
codes.student_help: The work solved for something slightly different from what the question asked.
codes.description: Gives a correct answer to a different target than the one asked.
codes.example: Asked for the probability of a carrier daughter, gives the probability of an affected son.

tell_apart.how: If the work was heading to the right target and stopped short, use PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION.
If a whole labelled part (b) is missing, use TST_SKIPPED_PART.

codes.remediation: Prompt deconstruction box: circle the verb, underline the target.

codes.name: Missing Units
codes.student_help: The final answer is missing its units.
codes.description: Omits units on a measurement answer.
codes.example: Writes the cell length as '25' with no µm.

tell_apart.how: If the number is wrong because of a conversion, use FAC_UNIT_CONVERSION.

codes.remediation: Unit slot habit: draw a box after the answer for the unit.

codes.name: Genetics Notation Error
codes.plain_name: Wrote alleles in a confusing way
codes.student_help: Use one letter per gene (capital = dominant) and write sex-linked alleles on the X, like Xᴴ.
codes.description: Right genetics in confusing notation: different letters for alleles of one gene, sex-linked alleles not written on X, no key for the symbols.
codes.example: Uses T for tall and s for short.

tell_apart.how: If the genotypes themselves are wrong, use STR_CROSS_SETUP.

codes.remediation: Tier 4: notation key template.

codes.name: Unsupported Answer
codes.student_help: The answer is there, but the reason the question asked for is missing.
codes.description: Gives an answer, claim or 'show that' conclusion without the reasoning or working the question requires.
codes.example: 'Will the cell shrink in salt water? Yes.' with no mention of osmosis.

tell_apart.how: COM_WORK_NOT_SHOWN is for missing calculation steps; this code is for a missing explanation in words.
If an explanation is there but uses loose words, use COM_IMPRECISE_TERMS.

codes.remediation: Claim-evidence-reasoning frame.

codes.name: Work Not Shown
codes.student_help: Write the formula, then the numbers in it, then the answer.
codes.description: A calculation answer with no formula, substitution or steps where the question expects them, so the method cannot be checked or credited.
codes.example: Writes 'actual size = 0.02 mm' with no calculation.

tell_apart.how: If the answer is wrong and there is no work, it is likely a guess: use TST_UNWORKED_GUESS. Use this code when the answer is right or close and only the steps are missing.
For a missing explanation in words, use COM_UNSUPPORTED_ANSWER.

codes.remediation: GRASS layout model: Given, Required, Analysis, Solution, Statement.

codes.name: Missing Labels / Definitions
codes.student_help: A graph, diagram or variable is missing labels, so it is unclear what it shows.
codes.description: Leaves out axis labels, scales, diagram labels or the 'let x be ...' definition that the work needs.
codes.example: Draws a plant cell with no labels.

tell_apart.how: COM_MISSING_UNITS is for a final numerical answer; this code is for diagrams, graphs and tables.

codes.remediation: Graph checklist card.

codes.name: Imprecise Terms
codes.plain_name: Used an everyday word where a subject term was needed
codes.student_help: Use the exact subject word instead of an everyday one.
codes.description: The idea is right but is stated with everyday or loose words where a specific scientific term is needed, so the answer is ambiguous.
codes.example: 'The food gets broken down by the juices' instead of naming enzymes.

tell_apart.how: If no reasoning is given at all, use COM_UNSUPPORTED_ANSWER.
If the wrong word shows a wrong idea (the student really thinks sugar melts in water), use the matching concept (CON) code instead.

codes.remediation: Word wall with paired everyday and scientific terms.

codes.name: Observation vs Inference
codes.plain_name: Mixed up what you saw with what it means
codes.student_help: Observations are what you saw, heard or measured; put explanations in the analysis.
codes.description: In lab or data questions, reports an explanation as if it were observed, or lists observations where an analysis or conclusion is asked for. Includes conclusions that go beyond the data.
codes.example: Observation: 'the yeast respired faster' when the record was balloon size.

tell_apart.how: STR_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN is about how the investigation is planned; this code is about how results are written up.

codes.remediation: Two-column observation / inference sort.

codes.name: Blank / Time Attrition
codes.student_help: This part was left blank.
codes.description: Leaves a question or part with no attempt, from time pressure or a frustration block.
codes.example: A whole question with no writing at all.

tell_apart.how: If any work was started, use TST_ABANDONED_WORK.
If other parts of the same question are answered, use TST_SKIPPED_PART.

codes.remediation: Prerequisite baseline probe on that topic.

codes.name: Skipped Part
codes.student_help: One part of the question was skipped while the others were answered.
codes.description: Answers some parts of a multi-part question and leaves another out, likely without noticing.
codes.example: Asked for genotype and phenotype ratios; gives only the genotype ratio.

tell_apart.how: If the whole question is empty, use TST_BLANK.
If the student answered something else instead of what was asked, use COM_ANSWERED_DIFFERENT_QUESTION.

codes.remediation: Part checklist habit.

codes.name: Distractor Trap
codes.plain_name: Middle step taken as the answer
codes.student_help: A middle step was treated as the final answer.
codes.description: Takes an intermediate value or a tempting wrong option as the final answer.
codes.example: Multiple choice on organelles: chooses 'nucleus' because it appeared in the stem.

tell_apart.how: If the work just stops, use PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION; this code is for presenting the wrong value as final.
If there is no work behind the choice, use TST_UNWORKED_GUESS.

codes.remediation: 'Is this what was asked?' stop sign.

codes.name: Abandoned Work
codes.student_help: A good start was stopped or crossed out before reaching an answer.
codes.description: Starts a valid approach, then stops or crosses it out partway with no answer.
codes.example: Starts the dihybrid square, fills four boxes, then stops.

tell_apart.how: If nothing was written, use TST_BLANK.
If the work reaches a result one step short of the target, use PRC_INCOMPLETE_SOLUTION.

codes.remediation: First-step confidence warm-up, then the same problem.

codes.name: Unchecked Answer
codes.student_help: A quick check would show this answer cannot be right, like a negative length.
codes.description: Gives an answer a quick check would show is impossible or absurd, and does not notice.
codes.example: Gives a probability of 150%.

tell_apart.how: Code the slip that caused the answer as well when it is visible; this code records that the impossible result was not caught.

codes.remediation: Estimate-then-check habit.

codes.name: Misread Given
codes.student_help: A number or sign in the question was read wrong.
codes.description: Misreads a number, sign or symbol printed in the question.
codes.example: Question says 100×; student uses 1000×.

tell_apart.how: If the slip happens between the student's own lines, use FAC_COPY_ERROR.

codes.remediation: Given-data check habit.

codes.name: Unworked Guess
codes.student_help: An answer was written with no working, and it is not right.
codes.description: Writes a wrong final answer with no working shown, suggesting a guess.
codes.example: Writes '3:1' with no square for a test-cross question; the answer is 1:1.

tell_apart.how: If the answer is right but the work is missing, use COM_WORK_NOT_SHOWN.

codes.remediation: Show-one-step routine.

codes.name: Reference Sheet Not Used
codes.student_help: If a value or formula is on the data sheet or periodic table, look it up instead of remembering it.
codes.description: Gets a value, constant or formula wrong that was printed on the provided data sheet, formula sheet or periodic table.
codes.example: Gets the amino acid for a codon wrong when the codon chart was provided.

tell_apart.how: If the formula or value was NOT provided, use the matching recall (FAC) code.

codes.remediation: Reference-sheet scavenger hunt before the test.
